memory_update.text: AEP is the strongest regulated-utility mapping in this chunk because its Ohio tariff and binding data-center MW disclosures create unusually concrete evidence for AI-related large-load demand.
GEV is the strongest equipment-vendor mapping because cached evidence ties Q1 2026 data-center orders directly to Electrification equipment and grid/generation bottleneck nodes.
D is a key regulated-utility mapping for Virginia/PJM data-center load, but cost-allocation and transmission upgrade treatment must be checked in regulatory filings before upgrading conviction.
TLN is a high-beta policy-test mapping for nuclear co-location and data-center firm-power procurement; its relationship is highly dependent on FERC/PJM treatment of co-located load.
ETN and PWR are plausible bottleneck suppliers for electrical equipment and grid EPC execution, but the current chunk needs direct order, backlog, lead-time, and customer-exposure evidence.
CEG is a credible firm-power/nuclear PPA mapping, but without verified signed hyperscaler contracts and incremental economics it should remain an inference rather than a fact-level relationship.
EXC, NI, XEL, and POR broaden the regulated-utility map beyond AEP and Dominion, but each needs docket-level tariff, cost-allocation, and customer-commitment verification.

HUBB is a lower-evidence, potentially less-obvious component supplier mapping; upgrade only if utility T&D component backlog and data-center/grid-modernization demand are directly supported by filings or management disclosures.

Need direct company filing checks for ETN, PWR, CEG, EXC, NI, XEL, POR, and HUBB before any Layer 2 ranking: segment exposure, backlog, customer concentration, tariff terms, regulatory dockets, signed contracts, and capex recovery.

Need market-pricing checks for all tickers in this chunk, including recent relative performance, valuation expansion, earnings revisions, short interest, and whether the AI power-grid narrative is already crowded.
Need FERC/PJM status verification as of June 2026 for co-located data-center load, network upgrade charges, generator-adjacent structures, and impacts on TLN, CEG, D, EXC, and AEP.

Need supplier lead-time and capacity evidence for transformers, switchgear, breakers, capacitors, substations, and EPC labor to separate true chokepoint beneficiaries from broad AI-infrastructure sympathy names.

summary: Mapped ticker relationships for a candidate Layer 2B chunk focused on AI data-center power access, large-load tariffs, grid interconnection, transmission capex, scarce electrical equipment, EPC execution capacity, and firm generation. The cleanest evidence-backed public-market mappings in this chunk are AEP for regulated grid-access/tariff exposure, GEV for grid and generation equipment bottlenecks, D for Virginia/PJM data-center load and cost-allocation exposure, and TLN for nuclear co-location policy risk. ETN, PWR, CEG, EXC, NI, XEL, POR, and HUBB remain relevant but require direct filing, backlog, tariff, customer, and regulatory verification before upgrading evidence quality.
